=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:4467-4491 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The replay subshell reads merge_commit_sha from stored JSON and passes it to git cherry-pick / rev-list without re-validating that it is still a valid, reachable commit.
  WHY: Corrupted or stale audit data can make replay fail in git; deepseek treated this as defense-in-depth, but the other reviewers still flagged the missing read-time validation.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:4139-4226 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The audit_unavailable path conflates “no prior audit exists yet” with “audit storage is unavailable,” producing a misleading skip/error message.
  WHY: First-time rebuilds and some memory-disabled cases surface as an ai-memory outage; deepseek disagreed on the first-time case and said the path is only misleading when memory is disabled, so the disagreement is about whether this blocks normal first-run rebuilds or just reports a confusing diagnostic.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:4347-4376 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Some _build_branch_rebuild_audit_json call sites pass an empty string for default_branch_head_sha, so the audit snapshot records null instead of the resolved base SHA.
  WHY: The persisted audit loses the forensic reference to the commit the rebuild was targeting; deepseek argued the empty-string cases were semantically correct when SHA resolution had not succeeded, so the disagreement is whether the cited call sites are truly after resolution.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:4398-4424 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The branch delete-then-recreate sequence is non-atomic and has no distributed lock or rebuild-in-progress sentinel.
  WHY: Concurrent poll ticks can observe or mutate a temporarily missing branch, causing transient ref errors or duplicate rebuild attempts; deepseek thought the cooldown gate makes the race unlikely, but the race window still exists.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:4227-4288 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The replay plan is recomputed from scratch on every attempt with no checkpoint for already replayed commits.
  WHY: After a partial rebuild failure, later attempts replay the same commits again and can conflict or create duplicate/empty commits; deepseek considered the duplicate-empty-commit effect cosmetic, while others reported terminal failures or repeated noise.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:4227-4288 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The replay-plan filter only includes `.status == "merged"`, so ready-to-merge/promoted wave issues can be omitted.
  WHY: If reconciliation has not advanced a just-merged sub-issue to the expected state, its commit never enters the rebuild plan and the rebuilt branch is incomplete.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:4347-4636 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The preflight-skip paths return success without updating STATE_FILE, so the audit says skipped_* while persistent state remains escalated.
  WHY: The state machine and audit diverge, and later ticks can re-enter or misreport the rebuild path instead of recording the specific skip reason.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:4467-4491 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The replay subshell uses numeric exit codes and relies on truncated log tails, with cleanup/error handling split across the subshell and outer wrapper.
  WHY: Diagnostics are opaque and the cleanup path is hard to reason about; some reviewers also noted that worktree cleanup can be missed or that the exit-code meaning is only implicit.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:4435-4440 | severity=medium | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: If mktemp/worktree allocation fails after the branch has already been recreated, the orchestrator marks the rebuild failed while leaving a clean branch in place.
  WHY: The state says failed but the ref exists at default_branch_head_sha with no replayed commits, creating a state/branch mismatch that could confuse later automation; deepseek considered the path extremely unlikely.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:4227-4288 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The GraphQL replay-metadata fetch is repeated on every considered rebuild without memoization.
  WHY: Repeated poll cycles pay the API/latency cost even when the branch is still gated by cooldown or otherwise won’t proceed; deepseek refuted this as threshold-gated, while others still reported repeated cost after escalation.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:4298-4314 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The new integration_sync_status token branch_rebuild_failed is added without documenting or explicitly handling it for downstream consumers.
  WHY: Old readers may treat the token as generic or unknown status, but the field change is additive and unlikely to break the poller itself.
- ai-memory/schemas/branch_rebuild_audit.v1.json:required array includes "branch_protected", "failure_detail", "completed_at" | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The audit schema marks nullable fields as required and shell builders sometimes emit empty strings where null is expected.
  WHY: Strict validators or downstream consumers can reject or misread otherwise valid audit records, and reviewers noted the null-versus-empty-string representation can diverge across toolchains.
- scripts/ai_memory.py:_read_json_object_file, _emit_branch_rebuild_audit_fallback, audit get/put helpers | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Memory validation/git/read failures fall back to warnings and partial JSON without durable error state.
  WHY: Repeated corruption or a missing memory branch can loop through fallback behavior without a persistent alert or sentinel, so operators may miss a real storage problem.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:_attempt_branch_rebuild_after_escalation variable scope usage (4347–4349, 4361, 4391) | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: BRANCH_REBUILD_ESCALATED_ERROR is shared without explicit local scoping, so future code could clobber the message.
  WHY: This is a maintainability hazard rather than an observed runtime failure; no current breakage was demonstrated.
- tests/test_branch_rebuild.py:1-124 | severity=low | confidence=1
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The file uses tab indentation throughout.
  WHY: The style differs from the spaces-used Python scripts but matches the existing tests/ convention, so no runtime issue; deepseek explicitly called the earlier inconsistency concern a false positive.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "add focused tests for threshold handling, cooldown enforcement, audit round-trip, and replay-failure behavior"
  expected_change_site: tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py and tests/test_branch_rebuild.py
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  EVIDENCE: The threshold, cooldown, audit round-trip, and replay-failure categories are present, but there is no happy-path rebuild test asserting threshold pass, cooldown pass, branch delete/recreate, cherry-pick replay, push success, and final healing-state assertions.
- requirement: "persist rebuild audit state on the ai-memory branch" / "persist branch_rebuild_audit.v1.json on the ai-memory branch, snapshot pre-rebuild state"
  expected_change_site: scripts/ai_memory.py, scripts/ai_memory_lib.py
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  EVIDENCE: The runtime paths still emit schema-violating or partial JSON, and fallback/error paths continue without a durable audit sentinel, so the audit contract is not fully satisfied on preflight or memory-failure paths.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: lines 4472-4473 (jq extraction of merge_commit_sha) and lines 4480-4485 (cherry-pick invocation) within the replay subshell
  Problem: The replay loop extracts merge_commit_sha from stored JSON and passes it directly to git cherry-pick and git rev-list without re-validating the SHA format or verifying the commit object exists in the already-fetched refs.
  Why it fails at runtime: If the SHA is syntactically valid but the commit object was garbage-collected or is inaccessible from the current fetch, git rev-list --parents returns empty (exit 22) or git cherry-pick fails (exit 23); the failure_detail surfaces the tail of replay_log, so this is a defense-in-depth gap rather than a current crash path.
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: _check_branch_rebuild_threshold function, lines 4169-4175 (audit_unavailable branch)
  Problem: When _branch_rebuild_audit_get returns failure, the function sets BRANCH_REBUILD_SKIP_REASON="audit_unavailable" and a message claiming the audit storage is unavailable.
  Why it fails at runtime: Deepseek judged the pass-1 “first-time rebuild” concern a false positive and said the message is accurate for memory-disabled / storage-unreachable cases, though it can still be misleading to operators.
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: _attempt_branch_rebuild_after_escalation function, lines 4358-4362 (skipped_missing_replay branch) and lines 4373-4376 (SHA resolution preflight skip)
  Problem: Passing "" as default_branch_head_sha is semantically correct when SHA resolution has not succeeded yet; this is not a bug.
  Why it fails at runtime: Deepseek concluded the pass-1 finding was a false positive because the SHA was never resolved in those branches, so null in the audit accurately reflects “unknown.”
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: _attempt_branch_rebuild_after_escalation function, lines 4398-4424 (delete + recreate sequence)
  Problem: The branch rebuild performs delete and recreate as separate API calls with no distributed lock.
  Why it fails at runtime: Deepseek considered same-project concurrency unlikely because the cooldown gate is checked before deletion and the audit write precedes delete, but it still identified a race window between the two API calls.
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: _derive_branch_rebuild_replay_commits function, lines 4227-4288
  Problem: The function recomputes the replay plan from all current merged wave issues every time it is
